newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak BSE to improve mkt efficiency, transparency.
newsitem.headline: Slovak BSE to improve mkt efficiency, transparency.

text.p: The Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) said on Wednesday that it plans to introduce long-awaited measures to improve market efficiency and transparency and bring bourse practices more in line with European standards.

Dusan Pavlik, chairman of the BSE chamber, told a news conference that the bourse would reduce the number of listed shares with "less liquid shares being transferred from the main to the unlisted market".
At present 15 issues are listed on the BSE main market out of 967 isssues registered on the bourse. Pavlik did not elaborate on the plan.
BSE chief executive Marian Sasik added that the BSE would also introduce stricter criteria for accepting listed issues and for registering shares on the unlisted market.
"We are now finalising the new rules which conform to European Union standards...the final version should be prepared next month" Sasik said.

Barbora Lazarova, head of the BSE listing commission, said the bourse would also introduce changes to the market's structure, including the creation of a third market -- in addition to the current listed and unlisted markets -- which would accept shares that met only the minimum criteria demanded by law.
Securities traders and foreign analysts have long complained that the Slovak capital market lacks transparency and gives little protection to minority shareholders.

Last month the World Bank recommended the exclusion of several illiquid shares from the bourse and creation of an independent supervisory body on the lines of the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC)
The BSE's main goal for the near future is to prepare for derivatives trading by the middle of this year, Sasik said.
But the BSE has yet to define products to be traded and work out legal proposals for such instruments, he added.
